chk_problem.label: accurate
chk_problem.poster_evidence: The construction industry remains one of the least automated sectors, despite its economic scale and high-risk tasks—especially on roofs. Roof work involves hazardous conditions like falls and repetitive physical labor, making it ideal for robotic automation. Quadruped robots, while increasingly capable, remain underutilized in real-world applications. This work investigates whether commercial quadrupeds like the Unitree Go2 can operate effectively on tiled roofs—a novel, unexplored environment combining steep inclines, smooth surfaces, and discrete structural features.
chk_problem.reason: The poster clearly describes the problem of automating hazardous roof work using quadruped robots in the 'Problem & Motivation' section.

chk_method.label: accurate
chk_method.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance.
chk_method.reason: The poster describes the method of building a custom roof test rig to evaluate the Unitree Go2 robot in the 'Experimental Setup' section.

chk_data.label: accurate
chk_data.poster_evidence: A custom test rig simulating a German-style tiled roof (Frankfurther Pfanne) was built to evaluate the Unitree Go2’s performance. Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers.
chk_data.reason: The poster mentions the Frankfurter Pfanne roof tiles and the OptiTrack motion capture system used to collect experimental data.

chk_setup.label: accurate
chk_setup.poster_evidence: Three core locomotion tasks were tested: balancing on increasing inclines, get-up/lie-down sequences in multiple orientations, and incline walking. Motion capture (OptiTrack) tracked foot slippage via reflective markers. Friction coefficients were measured using a UR10e force-torque sensor. All trials were automated via Python using WebRTC, with the robot set to standard walking mode at 1.0 m/s. Experiments were repeated 10 times per condition for statistical significance.
chk_setup.reason: The poster details the experimental setup, including the tasks, motion capture, Python automation, and speed of 1.0 m/s.

chk_primary_result.label: accurate
chk_primary_result.poster_evidence: Incline walking showed a quadratic increase in slippage with incline angle (p < 0.001), with critical failures occurring regularly at 25°. Even on flat ground, tile steps caused slippage. Regression analysis confirmed a linear decrease in traveled distance and no significant correlation with trajectory deviation. Friction coefficients were 1.144 (flat) and 1.430 (curved), suggesting theoretical inclines >48°, but dynamic performance fell far short—highlighting control and stability as key bottlenecks.
chk_primary_result.reason: The poster reports the quadratic increase in slippage, critical failures at 25 degrees, and the measured friction coefficients of 1.144 and 1.430.

chk_secondary_result.label: accurate
chk_secondary_result.poster_evidence: Standing balance failed at 27.58° ± 0.72°, primarily due to front-limb slippage. Get-up/lie-down succeeded only up to 11° (head-up/down) and 7° (sideways), failing when the center of mass exited the support polygon.
chk_secondary_result.reason: The poster reports the critical standing angle of 27.58° ± 0.72° and the get-up/lie-down success limits of 11° and 7°.

chk_baseline.label: accurate
chk_baseline.poster_evidence: The Go2 failed to meet manufacturer claims of 40° slope capability.
chk_baseline.reason: The poster compares the robot's performance against the manufacturer's claim of a 40-degree slope capability.

chk_conclusion.label: accurate
chk_conclusion.poster_evidence: but dynamic performance fell far short—highlighting control and stability as key bottlenecks. ... These findings call for co-design of hardware, control, and perception for roof-capable quadrupeds.
chk_conclusion.reason: The poster concludes that unmodified quadrupeds are not suited for roof environments and require significant co-design of hardware and control.

chk_limitation.label: accurate
chk_limitation.poster_evidence: Testing should expand to other platforms, variable speeds, weather conditions, and payloads.
chk_limitation.reason: The poster lists weather conditions and payloads as areas for future expansion, implying the current study's limitation of not testing under these conditions.
